newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-French temp agency could be on the market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French temp agency could be on the market.

text.p: The death of Bis SA's chairman and founder Laurent Negro has put the French temporary job agency in play, financial analysts said, predicting its shares could rise sharply when they resume trading next week.
Negro's death last weekend has revived speculation that the family-controlled firm may be a takeover target by a foreign temporary help agency looking for a strong French presence.
A Bis official said the company's shares, suspended Monday at 533 francs, would likely start trading again on Tuesday.

Analysts said the shares could hit and likely eclipse their 1996 high of 680 francs touched last June when Bis, capitalised at 2.5 billion francs ($480 million), was last the subject of takeover talk.

"It could rise to 680 or 700 on speculation alone," said Jean-Noel Vieille of brokerage Meeschaert-Rousselle. If a bid does surface, Annick Thevenon, analyst at EIFB, said an offer would likely be in the range of 700-800 francs per share.

She did not, however, rule out chances of a share swap like the one carried out last May between France's Ecco and Switzerland's Adia that spawned Adecco, Europe's biggest temporary personnel services firm.
A wave of international consolidation has been sweeping the temporary personnel sector amid growing demand by multinational companies for global recruitment services.

Analysts said Bis, whose profits have been suffering from weak employment demand in its home market, needs to find an international partner to expand into markets where job activity is stronger than in France, which is staggering under record 12.7 percent unemployment.
"It needs an international alliance to resolve its problems of a bad outlook in France," said Vieille.
Bis, almost exclusively focused on France, ranks third in the country with 13 percent market share. In second place is Adecco after U.S. giant Manpower with 29 percent, analysts said.
"It's a good opportunity for any foreign company with ambitions to have a strong foothold in France. There should be quite a few companies interested," said one Paris analyst.
Bis has appointed board member Claude Charbonniaud to succeed Negro, who pioneered temporary help services in France.
It said in a statement Charbonniaud "will direct the group continuing the policies defined" by Negro in 1996.
That means, the Bis official said, Bis would continue to seek an international partner. "This is an integral part (of our strategy)," he said. "It will be followed in the same fashion."
Bis announced last June a partnership would be sought through shareholder cross-holdings rather than a merger.
Asked whether the same scenario still applied, the Bis official told Reuters, "Things are a little different in that Negro's beneficiaries are not active in the business. It's a problem of capital.
"We need to find a solution to assure the future of Bis that also permits the family to preserve its interests," he said.
Negro and family members held around 60 percent of Bis.
The official said the quest for an international ally was "more advanced than in June" but it was premature to identify any potential partners.

Possible contenders for Bis are the Netherlands' Randstad Holding NV and Vendex International NV, which bought French cleaning company Bis Proprete, a unit of Bis, in 1995. U.S. Olsten Corp's name has also surfaced.
Neither Ranstad nor Vendex were available for comment.

Manpower, known to favour internal growth and outright acquisitions, was reported to have ruled itself out of the running for Bis. Adecco is seen an unlikely contender as it is still digesting the merger that created it.
Bis posted a first-half profit of 34 million francs, down from 70 million a year earlier, and forecast lower 1996 results.
($1=5.210 French Franc)
